name: Constitution Hill
subtitle: A former Johannesburg prison, closed in 1983, where South Africa's Constitutional Court opened on 21 March 2004.

facts.label: Kind
facts.value: Former prison precinct, museum and Constitutional Court

parts.text: Constitution Hill is a precinct in Johannesburg that opened in 1893 as a prison and closed in 1983. In the late 1990s and early 2000s it was revamped to become a museum, and in 2004 the Constitutional Court opened its doors there.
The prison doors to the Old Fort and to Number Four were officially closed on 31 January 1983.
A total of 156 people, among them Nelson Mandela and Oliver Tambo, were arrested and held at the complex before the Treason Trial of 1956.
In 1958 some 2,000 women, Winnie Madikizela-Mandela and Albertina Sisulu among them, were detained after protesting the pass laws.

sections.title: A court on the site of a prison

parts.text: In the mid-1990s the site was identified as the home of the new Constitutional Court.
On Human Rights Day, 21 March 2004, the Constitutional Court was inaugurated, and Constitution Hill opened to the public the next day.

gaps: Who built the Old Fort and why, and what the Women's Jail and the Awaiting Trial Block were. The site's history page does not say.
The prisoners' own accounts. The page names well-known detainees and numbers; the voices of ordinary prisoners are the part a visitor most needs, and this card does not have them.
What the Constitutional Court has decided and how the building was designed. Neither is covered by the sources read.
Whether and how it can be visited, guided tours and opening times. The site's pages were read for history only.
The coordinates are Wikipedia's for the precinct, not an entrance.
